body: Start with the thing that is actually broken, not the thing that is interesting to build.
evidence: Existing route planners all required drawing the path by hand. That was the problem worth solving, not the map rendering.

body: Write down what you expect to happen, and what result would prove you wrong, before writing code.
evidence: Framed a formal experiment first: null and alternative hypotheses, and a quantitative 90-day success threshold.

body: Build the smallest system that can answer the question. Constraints are a feature.
evidence: Zero-build architecture: pure HTML, CSS and JS, no framework, no npm — 22,000+ records served offline at zero hosting cost.

body: Instrument the funnel, not the vanity number. If you cannot attribute it, you cannot learn from it.
evidence: UTM attribution typed end to end, with an event schema tracking the full path from discovery through to the eBay redirect.

body: Put the decision point in the plan up front, so killing something is a scheduled outcome rather than an admission.
evidence: A 90-day decision gate built into the architecture, with the success threshold agreed before launch.
